column1: # Forever rules for the Warrior: the spec file of jvbastel/WOWAI#204. forever/generator makes the
# Forever DBC folder, the client data patch and the Forever server tables from it. Never edit a generated
# file by hand. To gather the data again, see forever/REFRESH.md.
#   Layout (tree, tier, column, ranks, prerequisite) and behaviour text: WoW Forever beta build 1.60.1.70450,
#     https://wow-forever.gg/talents/warrior/ (client data of build 1.60.1.70532; 0 spell and 0 talent changes since 70450)
#     Blizzard: class deep dive of 30 Sep 2026, beta development notes of 24 Sep to 15 Oct, Warrior update of 2 Oct.
#   Numbers (per-rank values, cooldowns, durations, costs, proc chances) and names: the local Forever client,
#   build 1.60.1.70685 (its talent and spell tables). Only numbers and names come from the client, never icons
#   Differences between the two builds: none in layout. The client settles Gore Drinker rank 1 at 0.5% (one fan
#   site shows 1%) and the Bloodthrill Overpower window at 5 sec (the deep dive says 6 sec).
#   Berserker Stance: the fan sites drop the 20% threat reduction from the text, but the client spell keeps
# Talent count of build 1.60.1.70450: 52 (Arms 17, Fury 17, Protection 18), 51 talent points.
# Free ID range: 60000-65535. A new talent, spell or skill line ability takes its ID from here. The stock
# 1.12.1 data ends at spell 33392, talent 1703 and skill line ability 15030, and spell IDs are SMALLINT
# UNSIGNED in the world database. Next free IDs: talent 60009, spell 60131.
#   A talent that survives in Forever keeps its 1.12 talent ID, and each of its ranks keeps the stock spell of
#   that rank: the Forever row replaces the stock spell by ID (the core with Forever.Rules = 1, and the client
#   data patch). A changed base ability does the same. So spell chains, trainers and the core code that knows a
#   spell by its ID keep working. A new talent, a new ability, or a rank that has no stock spell takes a new ID.
# Known differences from the text of #204 (the build data wins):
#   Recklessness keeps its 30 minute cooldown; only Retaliation and Shield Wall go to 15 minutes.
#   Bloodthirst gives movement speed, not attack speed.
#   Deep Wounds: the client has no crit flag on its bleed; #204 user story 12 lets its ticks crit (#214).
# Warrior mechanics (server code, src/game/Forever/ForeverWarrior*.{h,cpp}, #214). Blizzard has published no
# formula for them, and the client holds none (only marker spells such as Rule of Rage 1322574). Our choices:
#   Rage from a melee swing that hits = base weapon speed in sec x 3.46 (one-hand, unarmed at 2.0 sec) or x 4.5
#     (two-hand): the community measurement of the beta (Icy Veins; kami-labs: a 2.2 sec sword gives 7 per hit).
#     Damage, level and haste do not count. A crit gives x2 (Blizzard 2 Oct: +100%). An off-hand hit gives half
#     (our choice, as the normalized rage of TBC). A dodge or parry gives no rage (stock: 75% of the damage).
#     A fully absorbed swing gives none, as in stock; other direct damage gives none. Rate.Rage.Income counts.
#     Rage from damage taken stays stock (the fixed armor reduction of the 8 Oct notes has no published table).
#   Warrior DoT crits: a tick of the Warrior's own Rend or Deep Wound rolls the main hand melee crit chance
#     (plus crit chance talents of the spell) and deals x2, plus crit damage talents such as Impale. Ticks of
#     other classes, and Rend from items, never crit. The 1.12 combat log has no crit flag for a tick, so the
#     client shows the doubled number only.
#   Rend taps the creature when it is applied.
#   Deep Wounds: the bleed is 20/40/60% of the weapon's own average damage (no attack power), and a new bleed
#     rolls the damage that the old one had not dealt yet into its 4 ticks.
# Not in the spec (out of scope of #204): Expertise, the racial changes, Legacy perks, the "Talented" points and
# Dual Specialization. Text-only changes are no rows (Defensive Stance, Challenging and Intimidating Shout).
# Columns (tab-separated; "-" keeps the stock or source value):
#   kind            talent; ability (a new spell that no talent teaches); base (a changed stock spell)
#   talentId        the 1.12 talent ID, or a new one from the free range; 0 for ability and base rows
#   tree            arms, fury or protection; - for ability and base rows
#   tier, column    from 1; 0 for ability and base rows
#   ranks           the rank count (the spell count of an ability or base row)
#   requiredTalent  the talent ID of the one prerequisite, or 0
#   requiredRank    the rank of the prerequisite, from 1, or 0
#   name            the name of the talent and of its rank spells
#   icon            a stock 1.12 SpellIcon.dbc ID. A new or changed spell never takes an icon that the core uses
#                   as a spell marker (the generator refuses it)
#   port            data (spell data is enough), C++ (needs server code, the notes name the ticket) or
#                   substitute (a workaround, the notes say which)
#   spells          the spell ID of each rank, separated by commas
#   sourceSpells    the stock spell that each rank is a copy of; a kept or changed stock spell is its own source
#   effect1-3       the value of spell effect 1, 2 or 3 for each rank, separated by / (one value = every rank).
#                   Raw spell values: Rage in tenths, time in ms. The generator writes it as base points
#                   (value - 1) with die sides 1. An effect with no effect type holds a value for the text or
#   set             spell_template columns to change: name=value;name=value, a value per rank separated by /
#                   (see FIELDS in generator/forever_gen/spec.py; nameSubtext is the rank text, scriptName the
#                   server script, empty to drop the stock one; procEvent.<column> sets the
#                   forever_spell_proc_event row of rank 1, one value for all ranks). Learning keys (#212):
#                   skillLine=<skill line> gives a new spell a skill line ability with its own ID (spellbook
#                   tab, spell chain); supersededBy=<spell> its next rank (default the next spell of the row);
#                   baseline=1 makes the core teach it at its spellLevel with no trainer
#   tooltip         the description of the rank spells; $s1 is the value of effect 1 ($h the proc chance)
#   notes           the Forever change and what is left for which ticket
